newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to sweep food factories after cholera outbreak.
newsitem.headline: HK to sweep food factories after cholera outbreak.

text.p: Health authorities in Hong Kong will launch a sweep on hundreds of food factories following an outbreak of cholera which was traced to contaminated poultry feet, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
The disease has struck eight people in the past week and some were found to have eaten chicken and duck feet produced by a factory in Yuen Long district, the government said.
"There are eight confirmed cases so far, and one, a 76 year old male, is in critical condition," the spokesman said, adding that there was another person suspected to have the disease.
Health officials on Wednesday seized 4,500 kg of chicken and duck feet from the fly-infested Yuen Long factory and ordered it to disinfect a well on its premises.
The factory defrosted meat and washed dishes with well water which was believed to be contaminated by sewage from staff toilets, health officials said.
Chicken and duck feet, cooked in a variety of ways, are favourite snacks in the territory.

"The Regional Services Department will check thoroughly all 499 food processing factories...within one to two weeks to safeguard public health in the wake of the recent spate of cholera cases," the government said.
